newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan President to send roses to Madame Chiang.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan President to send roses to Madame Chiang.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui will send 100 red roses to Madame Chiang Kai-shek, widow of the nationalist leader, to celebrate her upcoming 100th birthday, a local newspaper said on Saturday.
The roses would be delivered by Jason Hu, Taipei's representative in the United States, on behalf of Lee, along with a birthday card and gifts, the United Evening News reported from New York.
Madame Chiang, who captivated the American public during World War Two and appealed passionately to the United States Congress for help against the occupying Japanese, will be 100 on March 20.
The ruling Nationalist Party said on Saturday it would send a high-ranking delegation to New York for Madame Chiang's birthday.
The former first lady currently lives on Long Island, New York, and rarely appears in public.
Chiang Kai-shek fled to Taiwan in 1949 after his Nationalist troops lost a civil war on mainland China to Mao Zedong's Red Army.
The Chiang family's power began to fade in Taiwan in 1988 with the death of President Chiang Ching-kuo, Chiang Kai-shek's son from a previous marriage.
